methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $5.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Rapidus is a late-stage semiconductor company that has raised $5.0B+ to date. The valuation framework drew on a peer universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-chip competitors including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. The peer-median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow chip design segment—12 same-sector peers exist, but fewer than 3 met the stage and tier filters required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring could not be executed because Rapidus, like most private companies, does not disclose revenue, precluding a price-to-sales multiple application to the 21.0x median observed across the three public semiconductor names.

Stage-progression analysis applied a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage advancement, yielding $6.0B from the $5.0B raised proxy. This single-method result supports a median valuation of $6.0B, with a triangulated range of $5.1B (low) to $6.9B (high). Key uncertainties remain: the absence of disclosed financials limits precision; comparable late-stage chip ventures at similar funding levels are sparse; and the frontier-chip sector's rapid technical and competitive evolution creates material visibility risk beyond traditional stage-based progression.
